category: 5. Browser-native layout, typography, and interface capabilities
name: CSS Grid
function: Two-dimensional layouts, editorial grids, dashboards.
tradeoff: Maintain meaningful DOM order across visual rearrangements.

category: 5. Browser-native layout, typography, and interface capabilities
name: Flexbox
function: One-dimensional alignment and distribution of controls/content.
tradeoff: Handle wrapping and minimum-content sizing deliberately.

category: 5. Browser-native layout, typography, and interface capabilities
name: Subgrid
function: Align nested cards and sections to parent grid tracks.
tradeoff: Excellent for aligned card metadata; nested grid structure still matters.

category: 5. Browser-native layout, typography, and interface capabilities
name: Container queries
function: Recompose a reusable component based on its container.
tradeoff: Size, style, scroll-state, and anchored query support are distinct.

category: 5. Browser-native layout, typography, and interface capabilities
name: CSS anchor positioning
function: Position tethered UI relative to a trigger, with fallback positions.
tradeoff: Geometry does not supply complete keyboard or popup semantics.

category: 5. Browser-native layout, typography, and interface capabilities
name: Logical properties
function: Direction-aware padding, margin, sizes, and positioning.
tradeoff: Test actual RTL content; directional icons may need separate treatment.

category: 5. Browser-native layout, typography, and interface capabilities
name: Cascade layers
function: Define intentional precedence across resets, libraries, themes, utilities.
tradeoff: Learn how unlayered styles and important declarations interact.

category: 5. Browser-native layout, typography, and interface capabilities
name: CSS nesting
function: Group related selectors within native CSS.
tradeoff: Avoid excessive nesting and accidental specificity.

category: 5. Browser-native layout, typography, and interface capabilities
name: CSS scope
function: Limit styling to a DOM subtree, optionally with boundaries.
tradeoff: MDN identifies newly available support; account for older clients.

category: 5. Browser-native layout, typography, and interface capabilities
name: :has()
function: Style a container based on related descendant/sibling state.
tradeoff: Prefer bounded selectors; do not replace necessary application state management.

category: 5. Browser-native layout, typography, and interface capabilities
name: Custom properties
function: Runtime theme, density, motion, and component tokens.
tradeoff: Naming, scope, and fallbacks need design-system governance.

category: 5. Browser-native layout, typography, and interface capabilities
name: @property
function: Register typed CSS custom properties for interpolation and defaults.
tradeoff: Registration does not make an expensive paint effect free.

category: 5. Browser-native layout, typography, and interface capabilities
name: clamp(), min(), max()
function: Bounded fluid type, spacing, and layouts.
tradeoff: Use sensible min/max and zoom-safe units; inspect extreme widths.

category: 5. Browser-native layout, typography, and interface capabilities
name: Dynamic/small viewport units
function: Fit browser chrome changes and mobile viewport conditions.
tradeoff: Choose dvh/svh/lvh deliberately; test keyboard and address-bar behavior.

category: 5. Browser-native layout, typography, and interface capabilities
name: Safe-area environment variables
function: Keep controls clear of device cutouts and system areas.
tradeoff: Combine with platform/webview configuration; do not assume one inset everywhere.

category: 5. Browser-native layout, typography, and interface capabilities
name: Overscroll behavior
function: Control scroll chaining at nested boundaries.
tradeoff: Preserve useful browser/navigation behavior and touch expectations.

category: 5. Browser-native layout, typography, and interface capabilities
name: Scroll anchoring
function: Stabilize reading position as content above changes.
tradeoff: Disable only for a demonstrated conflict; virtual lists need coordination.

category: 5. Browser-native layout, typography, and interface capabilities
name: Scrollbar gutter
function: Reserve scrollbar space and reduce width jumps.
tradeoff: Overlay-scrollbar platforms behave differently.

category: 5. Browser-native layout, typography, and interface capabilities
name: Variable fonts
function: Multiple weights, widths, or custom axes in a font resource.
tradeoff: One variable font is not always smaller than the few static styles you need.

category: 5. Browser-native layout, typography, and interface capabilities
name: Optical sizing
function: Size-specific letterforms when the font supports an optical axis.
tradeoff: Depends on the chosen font, not just browser support.

category: 5. Browser-native layout, typography, and interface capabilities
name: Numeric OpenType variants
function: Tabular numbers, fractions, ordinals, and other numeric glyph choices.
tradeoff: Font must contain the requested features.

category: 5. Browser-native layout, typography, and interface capabilities
name: text-wrap
function: Balanced headings and improved wrapping via supported values.
tradeoff: Balance/pretty/stable differ; test per-value support and layout cost.

category: 5. Browser-native layout, typography, and interface capabilities
name: font-size-adjust
function: Improve apparent size consistency between preferred/fallback fonts.
tradeoff: Does not alone match all ascent, descent, width, and line-gap metrics.

category: 5. Browser-native layout, typography, and interface capabilities
name: Font metric overrides
function: Tune fallback size alongside ascent/descent/line-gap descriptors.
tradeoff: Values must be derived for the actual font pair.

category: 5. Browser-native layout, typography, and interface capabilities
name: Fontsource
function: Versioned packages for self-hosting open-source fonts.
tradeoff: Select only required files; verify font-specific licenses and scripts.

category: 5. Browser-native layout, typography, and interface capabilities
name: Utopia
function: Generates fluid type and space scales.
tradeoff: Generated values are a starting point; inspect real content and zoom.

category: 5. Browser-native layout, typography, and interface capabilities
name: Google Fonts
function: Font discovery and delivery ecosystem.
tradeoff: Review individual font licensing, privacy needs, and delivery strategy.

category: 5. Browser-native layout, typography, and interface capabilities
name: Adobe Fonts
function: Commercial font discovery and licensed activation/web use.
tradeoff: Subscription and web hosting/embedding rights require project-specific review.

category: 5. Browser-native layout, typography, and interface capabilities
name: OKLCH
function: Perceptually oriented lightness/chroma/hue color specification.
tradeoff: Check gamut mapping and contrast on actual rendered colors.

category: 5. Browser-native layout, typography, and interface capabilities
name: Relative CSS colors
function: Derive themed color variations from base tokens.
tradeoff: Derived colors still need contrast checks; use fallbacks as necessary.

category: 5. Browser-native layout, typography, and interface capabilities
name: color-mix()
function: Blend colors in a chosen interpolation space.
tradeoff: A convenient blend is not automatically an accessible palette.

category: 5. Browser-native layout, typography, and interface capabilities
name: Culori
function: Color conversion, interpolation, and gamut-aware calculations in JS.
tradeoff: Use when programmatic color work exceeds native CSS needs.

category: 5. Browser-native layout, typography, and interface capabilities
name: Color.js
function: Color-space conversion, color manipulation, and contrast-related utilities.
tradeoff: Match chosen contrast algorithms to your actual compliance target.

category: 5. Browser-native layout, typography, and interface capabilities
name: HTML dialog
function: Native modal/nonmodal dialog foundation.
tradeoff: Add proper names, initial focus, close behavior, and focus restoration; subfeatures vary.

category: 5. Browser-native layout, typography, and interface capabilities
name: Popover API
function: Declarative/scripted top-layer popovers and supported dismissal behavior.
tradeoff: Popovers are nonmodal; choose appropriate roles and focus behavior.

category: 5. Browser-native layout, typography, and interface capabilities
name: Native select
function: OS-integrated option selection with established behavior.
tradeoff: New customizable-select features have separate compatibility requirements.

category: 5. Browser-native layout, typography, and interface capabilities
name: details / summary
function: Native disclosure foundation for FAQ and secondary information.
tradeoff: Not a substitute for every tab, menu, or complex tree interaction.

category: 5. Browser-native layout, typography, and interface capabilities
name: inert
function: Make a subtree unavailable to focus and interaction.
tradeoff: Coordinate visual state and restoration; do not strand focus.

category: 5. Browser-native layout, typography, and interface capabilities
name: Intl
function: Locale-aware numbers, dates, plurals, lists, collation, segmentation.
tradeoff: Translation and product terminology need a separate content workflow.

category: 5. Browser-native layout, typography, and interface capabilities
name: FormatJS
function: Internationalized messages and ICU-format tooling.
tradeoff: Plan message extraction and translator context.

category: 5. Browser-native layout, typography, and interface capabilities
name: i18next
function: Translation resources, language resolution, framework integrations.
tradeoff: Test plural rules, fallbacks, interpolation, and layout expansion.

category: 5. Browser-native layout, typography, and interface capabilities
name: Lingui
function: Message catalog and compile-time localization workflow.
tradeoff: Align extraction and build configuration with the app.

category: 5. Browser-native layout, typography, and interface capabilities
name: DTCG design-token format
function: Shared representation for typed design decisions across tooling.
tradeoff: Stable community-group format exists; actual tool interoperability still needs validation.

category: 6. Motion, transitions, graphics, and creative rendering
name: CSS transitions
function: Interpolates property changes; ideal for small hover, focus, toggle, and pressed feedback.
tradeoff: Explicitly name properties; `transition: all` can animate unrelated layout changes.

category: 6. Motion, transitions, graphics, and creative rendering
name: CSS keyframe animations
function: Repeating or staged CSS animation; loaders, short entrances, ambient accents.
tradeoff: Pause unnecessary loops; honor reduced motion and avoid making content depend on animation.

category: 6. Motion, transitions, graphics, and creative rendering
name: Web Animations API
function: JavaScript control of keyframes, playback, reversal, cancellation, and animation timing.
tradeoff: Low dependency cost, but you own orchestration, lifecycle cleanup, and feature differences.

category: 6. Motion, transitions, graphics, and creative rendering
name: View Transition API
function: Browser-managed snapshots and shared visual continuity for state changes and page navigation.
tradeoff: Check same-document and cross-document support separately; retain focus, history, and nonanimated navigation.

category: 6. Motion, transitions, graphics, and creative rendering
name: CSS scroll-driven animations
function: Drives animation progress from scrolling or element visibility; progress bars and restrained reveals.
tradeoff: Test the exact timeline/range feature on target browsers; preserve the full static layout.

category: 6. Motion, transitions, graphics, and creative rendering
name: ScrollTimeline / ViewTimeline
function: Uses scroll/view progress as an animation timeline through JavaScript.
tradeoff: Related to M005, not a separate library; older devices still need fallback.

category: 6. Motion, transitions, graphics, and creative rendering
name: CSS `linear()` easing
function: Piecewise easing curves, including sampled spring-like curves, without a runtime physics engine.
tradeoff: A sampled curve has fixed playback; use a real spring for velocity-sensitive retargeting.

category: 6. Motion, transitions, graphics, and creative rendering
name: `@starting-style`
function: Supplies entry styles for newly rendered elements, useful with dialog/popover transitions.
tradeoff: Baseline 2024 in inspected docs; coordinate entry/exit/display/top-layer behavior and verify older targets.

category: 6. Motion, transitions, graphics, and creative rendering
name: `transition-behavior: allow-discrete`
function: Allows transitions involving discrete properties such as `display`.
tradeoff: MDN marks limited availability in the inspected page; keep a working immediate-state fallback.

category: 6. Motion, transitions, graphics, and creative rendering
name: `interpolate-size`
function: Opts into transitions between explicit sizes and supported intrinsic size values.
tradeoff: Experimental/limited availability in inspected docs; size animation can still incur layout work.

category: 6. Motion, transitions, graphics, and creative rendering
name: CSS motion paths
function: Moves elements along a path through offset properties; useful for diagrams or decorative trajectories.
tradeoff: Essential information should remain understandable without following motion.

category: 6. Motion, transitions, graphics, and creative rendering
name: CSS Scroll Snap
function: Native alignment of scrolling galleries and stepwise panels.
tradeoff: Aggressive mandatory snapping can impede exploration; test keyboard, touch, and long content.

category: 6. Motion, transitions, graphics, and creative rendering
name: `requestAnimationFrame`
function: Schedules custom drawing and animation work around browser frames.
tradeoff: Use elapsed time, not fixed per-frame increments; cancel loops on teardown.

category: 6. Motion, transitions, graphics, and creative rendering
name: Pointer Events
function: Common mouse, pen, and touch input model, including capture for dragging.
tradeoff: Pointer handling does not provide keyboard alternatives or accessibility semantics.

category: 6. Motion, transitions, graphics, and creative rendering
name: WebGPU
function: GPU graphics and compute for demanding rendering and simulation.
tradeoff: Requires secure context and supported browser/device; handle adapter failure/device loss and supply fallback.

category: 6. Motion, transitions, graphics, and creative rendering
name: OffscreenCanvas
function: Allows canvas rendering away from the DOM and, where supported, in workers.
tradeoff: Worker rendering reduces some main-thread pressure; it does not reduce GPU or asset costs automatically.

category: 6. Motion, transitions, graphics, and creative rendering
name: GSAP core
function: Tweens JavaScript properties, DOM styles, SVG, and scene values; coordinates timelines and callbacks.
tradeoff: Strong general orchestration; lifecycle cleanup and property ownership remain your responsibility.

category: 6. Motion, transitions, graphics, and creative rendering
name: ScrollTrigger
function: Scroll-linked timelines, pinning, scrubbing, snapping, and triggers.
tradeoff: Pinning consumes scroll distance; refresh measurements after relevant layout/font changes.

category: 6. Motion, transitions, graphics, and creative rendering
name: ScrollSmoother
function: Adds transformed-content smoothing and parallax on top of native scrolling and ScrollTrigger.
tradeoff: Requires ScrollTrigger and a suitable wrapper; test fixed elements, anchors, keyboard, and touch.

category: 6. Motion, transitions, graphics, and creative rendering
name: ScrollToPlugin
function: Animates scroll destinations.
tradeoff: Leave user interruption possible; native scrolling is sufficient for many anchor links.

category: 6. Motion, transitions, graphics, and creative rendering
name: SplitText
function: Splits lines/words/characters for text animation; supports responsive re-splitting and ARIA assistance.
tradeoff: Preserve nested link semantics; split only necessary content and avoid delaying hero comprehension.

category: 6. Motion, transitions, graphics, and creative rendering
name: ScrambleTextPlugin
function: Scrambles characters into final text.
tradeoff: Decorative short labels only; retain an accessible stable text equivalent.

category: 6. Motion, transitions, graphics, and creative rendering
name: TextPlugin
function: Replaces text progressively.
tradeoff: Avoid announcing every intermediate change to screen readers.

category: 6. Motion, transitions, graphics, and creative rendering
name: DrawSVGPlugin
function: Reveals SVG strokes progressively, including selected segments.
tradeoff: Acts on strokes, not filled shapes; dense paths can be expensive.

category: 6. Motion, transitions, graphics, and creative rendering
name: MorphSVGPlugin
function: Interpolates SVG path shapes.
tradeoff: Choose readable start/end shapes; complex geometry still needs optimization.

category: 6. Motion, transitions, graphics, and creative rendering
name: MotionPathPlugin
function: Animates along paths with orientation.
tradeoff: A guided path should communicate relationships; looping particles can distract.

category: 6. Motion, transitions, graphics, and creative rendering
name: MotionPathHelper
function: Visually edits motion paths.
tradeoff: Authoring aid; do not unnecessarily ship editing controls to visitors.

category: 6. Motion, transitions, graphics, and creative rendering
name: Flip
function: Animates between measured layout states, including DOM reordering and shared-element changes.
tradeoff: Capture before/after layout at the correct framework lifecycle point; avoid concurrent measurements.

category: 6. Motion, transitions, graphics, and creative rendering
name: Draggable
function: Dragging, bounds, rotation, and snapping controls.
tradeoff: Supply click/keyboard alternatives and discoverable handles.

category: 6. Motion, transitions, graphics, and creative rendering
name: InertiaPlugin
function: Momentum and settling after release.
tradeoff: Companion to interactions such as Draggable; limit excessive travel and settling time.

category: 6. Motion, transitions, graphics, and creative rendering
name: Observer
function: Normalizes wheel/touch/pointer gesture observations.
tradeoff: Do not intercept ordinary navigation gestures without a clear interaction purpose.

category: 6. Motion, transitions, graphics, and creative rendering
name: CustomEase
function: Custom timing curves.
tradeoff: Establish a small shared vocabulary rather than unique easing on every control.

category: 6. Motion, transitions, graphics, and creative rendering
name: CustomWiggle
function: Configurable oscillating eases.
tradeoff: Requires CustomEase; limit to intentional character or feedback moments.

category: 6. Motion, transitions, graphics, and creative rendering
name: CustomBounce
function: Configurable bounce eases.
tradeoff: Requires CustomEase; repeated bounce is distracting in task interfaces.

category: 6. Motion, transitions, graphics, and creative rendering
name: EasePack
function: Additional RoughEase, SlowMo, and ExpoScaleEase curves.
tradeoff: Specialized expression; only import what the scene uses.

category: 6. Motion, transitions, graphics, and creative rendering
name: Physics2DPlugin
function: Velocity/acceleration-style 2D motion.
tradeoff: A motion helper, not a complete collision simulation engine.

category: 6. Motion, transitions, graphics, and creative rendering
name: PhysicsPropsPlugin
function: Physics-like interpolation of properties.
tradeoff: Use a full physics engine only when bodies, contacts, or constraints are required.

category: 6. Motion, transitions, graphics, and creative rendering
name: GSDevTools
function: Playback and timeline inspection controls.
tradeoff: Development tool; keep it out of the final public interface.

category: 6. Motion, transitions, graphics, and creative rendering
name: PixiPlugin
function: GSAP integration for Pixi display properties.
tradeoff: Useful only in a Pixi scene; check supported Pixi major versions.

category: 6. Motion, transitions, graphics, and creative rendering
name: `useGSAP`
function: React integration with scoped setup and cleanup via GSAP context.
tradeoff: Ensure callbacks and subsequently created animations are also cleaned up.

category: 6. Motion, transitions, graphics, and creative rendering
name: Motion
function: Animation, springs, layout transitions, gestures, presence, and scroll tools for React/JS/Vue.
tradeoff: Choose the appropriate platform API; avoid mounting/unmounting that prevents exit animation.

category: 6. Motion, transitions, graphics, and creative rendering
name: Anime.js
function: Framework-independent tweens, timelines, SVG/text tools, draggable and layout capabilities, WAAPI tooling.
tradeoff: Check current-major APIs; older tutorials may describe a different API surface.

category: 6. Motion, transitions, graphics, and creative rendering
name: react-spring
function: Spring-driven React animation with several rendering targets.
tradeoff: Tune damping and interruption carefully; long oscillations are rarely helpful for frequent actions.

category: 6. Motion, transitions, graphics, and creative rendering
name: AutoAnimate
function: Automatically animates immediate-child insertions, removals, and reordering.
tradeoff: Convenient for lists; less precise than authored choreography and affects layout context.

category: 6. Motion, transitions, graphics, and creative rendering
name: Lenis
function: Optional scroll smoothing and synchronization for visual experiences.
tradeoff: Native CSS scroll-snap is unsupported per its README; use its snap integration if needed. Test anchors, focus, and reduced motion.

category: 6. Motion, transitions, graphics, and creative rendering
name: Locomotive Scroll
function: Scroll-based viewport detection, smooth scrolling, and parallax; the current repository builds on Lenis.
tradeoff: Check the installed major; current documentation and old transform-scroller tutorials differ.

category: 6. Motion, transitions, graphics, and creative rendering
name: use-gesture
function: Drag, pinch, wheel, hover, and related gesture state for custom interactions.
tradeoff: Gesture recognition is separate from rendering and keyboard accessibility.

category: 6. Motion, transitions, graphics, and creative rendering
name: Rive
function: Authored interactive graphics, timelines, state-driven behavior, data binding, and runtime delivery.
tradeoff: Budget runtime plus assets; provide semantic HTML/native controls around visual interactions.

category: 6. Motion, transitions, graphics, and creative rendering
name: Lottie Web
function: Plays exported vector animation, commonly from After Effects workflows.
tradeoff: Exported feature support varies; huge path counts or raster assets undermine lightweight delivery.

category: 6. Motion, transitions, graphics, and creative rendering
name: dotLottie runtimes
function: Packages and plays Lottie assets across web/mobile integrations.
tradeoff: Format, runtime, state-machine support, and framework wrapper are separate version choices.

category: 6. Motion, transitions, graphics, and creative rendering
name: Theatre.js
function: Visual keyframe/curve authoring for JavaScript values and 3D sequences.
tradeoff: Strong for art direction; inspect current package compatibility before building a new production pipeline.

category: 6. Motion, transitions, graphics, and creative rendering
name: Barba.js
function: Coordinates transitions between website pages.
tradeoff: Own focus, analytics, scripts, caching, and back/forward behavior; compare native View Transitions first.

category: 6. Motion, transitions, graphics, and creative rendering
name: Swup
function: Extensible page transitions for server-rendered sites.
tradeoff: Test progressive enhancement and third-party script lifecycle after content replacement.

category: 6. Motion, transitions, graphics, and creative rendering
name: Svelte transitions / animate
function: Framework-native entry/exit and movement animation.
tradeoff: Usually the simplest fit for Svelte; avoid adding a second engine for equivalent needs.

category: 6. Motion, transitions, graphics, and creative rendering
name: Vue Transition / TransitionGroup
function: Framework-native transition lifecycle and list movement.
tradeoff: Supply transition styles and cancellation behavior; visual motion does not supply component semantics.

category: 6. Motion, transitions, graphics, and creative rendering
name: Motion Studio / AI Kit / Performance Doctor
function: Official authoring and agent-oriented tools for creating and diagnosing Motion work.
tradeoff: Tool-assisted diagnosis needs real-browser validation; access/plan terms should be checked.

category: 6. Motion, transitions, graphics, and creative rendering
name: Three.js
function: 3D scenes, cameras, meshes, lighting, materials, loaders, animation, and renderers.
tradeoff: A rendering toolkit: you still design interaction, accessibility, asset budgets, and quality tiers.

category: 6. Motion, transitions, graphics, and creative rendering
name: Three.js WebGPURenderer
function: Renderer selecting WebGPU where available and falling back to WebGL2.
tradeoff: Renderer fallback does not guarantee every custom shader or compute feature has an equivalent fallback.

category: 6. Motion, transitions, graphics, and creative rendering
name: Three.js TSL
function: Node-based shader authoring within the Three ecosystem.
tradeoff: Check renderer/material compatibility; existing GLSL ShaderMaterial code may require migration.

category: 6. Motion, transitions, graphics, and creative rendering
name: React Three Fiber
function: Declarative React renderer for Three.js, integrating scene composition and React state.
tradeoff: Pair React and Fiber major versions correctly; inspected docs mark v10 as alpha.

category: 6. Motion, transitions, graphics, and creative rendering
name: Drei
function: R3F helpers for controls, environment, text, assets, instances, and adaptive rendering.
tradeoff: Helpers can contain expensive effects; evaluate each selected component rather than enabling everything.

category: 6. Motion, transitions, graphics, and creative rendering
name: Babylon.js
function: Broad web rendering engine with integrated scene tooling and ecosystem.
tradeoff: Attractive for substantial 3D applications; a simple model preview may need less infrastructure.

category: 6. Motion, transitions, graphics, and creative rendering
name: PlayCanvas
function: WebGL/WebGPU engine and collaborative editor for interactive 3D.
tradeoff: Engine and hosted editor are separate product choices; inspect project/export requirements.

category: 6. Motion, transitions, graphics, and creative rendering
name: Spline
function: Visual creation and publishing of interactive 3D and 2D scenes; animation, materials, events, and data.
tradeoff: Inspect embed size, loading, ownership/export options, and device performance for the chosen plan.

category: 6. Motion, transitions, graphics, and creative rendering
name: Spline Hana
function: Spline's 2D interface/animated-graphics editor sharing its interaction and publishing model.
tradeoff: A visual authoring option; exported canvas does not automatically provide accessible document structure.

category: 6. Motion, transitions, graphics, and creative rendering
name: `<model-viewer>`
function: Web component for interactive model presentation and supported AR modes.
tradeoff: AR capabilities vary by device; provide poster, loading/error states, and non-AR access.

category: 6. Motion, transitions, graphics, and creative rendering
name: OGL
function: Minimal WebGL abstraction for custom graphics and shader-driven scenes.
tradeoff: Less built-in infrastructure means more renderer/asset work for the developer.

category: 6. Motion, transitions, graphics, and creative rendering
name: Curtains.js
function: Positions WebGL image/video/canvas planes relative to DOM elements.
tradeoff: Useful for image distortions and transitions; handle resize, scroll, context loss, and static fallbacks.

category: 6. Motion, transitions, graphics, and creative rendering
name: PixiJS
function: GPU-based 2D scene graph, textures, text, events, filters, masks, and particles.
tradeoff: Canvas graphics require explicit accessibility treatment; measure GPU overdraw and texture memory.

category: 6. Motion, transitions, graphics, and creative rendering
name: Konva
function: Canvas scene graph with input, layers, dragging, transforms, filters, and raster export.
tradeoff: Good for editors and diagrams; manage redraws, large scenes, and accessible alternatives.

category: 6. Motion, transitions, graphics, and creative rendering
name: Fabric.js
function: Interactive canvas objects, rich text editing, serialization, SVG import/export, and custom controls.
tradeoff: Export fidelity, font availability, and migration across major versions need testing.

category: 6. Motion, transitions, graphics, and creative rendering
name: p5.js
function: Creative coding for interactive art, animation, and visual experiments.
tradeoff: Excellent exploration tool; production interfaces still need accessibility and resource budgets.

category: 6. Motion, transitions, graphics, and creative rendering
name: Paper.js
function: Vector graphics and path operations on canvas; illustration and geometry tools.
tradeoff: Verify current release/maintenance before new adoption; not interchangeable with Paper Shaders.

category: 6. Motion, transitions, graphics, and creative rendering
name: Two.js
function: Common 2D drawing abstraction across SVG, Canvas, and WebGL renderers.
tradeoff: Renderer differences and project maintenance should be checked for required features.

category: 6. Motion, transitions, graphics, and creative rendering
name: Rapier
function: 2D/3D rigid-body physics, contacts, constraints, and scene queries with web bindings.
tradeoff: Physics consumes CPU/WASM startup; use fixed stepping and limit active bodies.

category: 6. Motion, transitions, graphics, and creative rendering
name: React Three Rapier
function: React/R3F integration for Rapier bodies, colliders, and events.
tradeoff: Match dependency versions; avoid React rerenders for every physics-frame update.

category: 6. Motion, transitions, graphics, and creative rendering
name: Matter.js
function: JavaScript 2D rigid-body simulation with collisions and constraints.
tradeoff: Useful for playful 2D interactions; unnecessary for ordinary button or panel springs.

category: 6. Motion, transitions, graphics, and creative rendering
name: pmndrs postprocessing
function: Three.js image effects and effect composition.
tradeoff: Bloom, depth effects, and additional passes increase GPU cost; inspect renderer compatibility.

category: 6. Motion, transitions, graphics, and creative rendering
name: Paper Shaders
function: Reusable canvas shader effects such as grain gradients, glass, dithering, water, and liquid metal.
tradeoff: Distinctive accents can become visual noise; pause offscreen and cap resolution.

category: 6. Motion, transitions, graphics, and creative rendering
name: TypeGPU
function: TypeScript-oriented WebGPU toolkit with typed GPU data and shader authoring.
tradeoff: Specialized graphics/compute infrastructure; budget for evolving APIs and device support.

category: 6. Motion, transitions, graphics, and creative rendering
name: glTF Transform
function: SDK/CLI for optimizing and processing glTF assets, geometry, animation, and textures.
tradeoff: Validate final visual quality and required loader/decoder support after compression.

category: 6. Motion, transitions, graphics, and creative rendering
name: Meshoptimizer
function: Mesh optimization, simplification, and compression for geometry pipelines.
tradeoff: Compression changes transfer/decoding tradeoffs; measure total startup cost.

category: 6. Motion, transitions, graphics, and creative rendering
name: Draco
function: Compresses 3D geometry for asset delivery.
tradeoff: Adds decoding work; compare with Meshopt using representative assets.

category: 6. Motion, transitions, graphics, and creative rendering
name: KTX / Basis Universal
function: Texture compression/transcoding pipeline for more efficient GPU texture delivery.
tradeoff: Format support, decoding, quality, and color management require validation.

category: 6. Motion, transitions, graphics, and creative rendering
name: tsParticles
function: Configurable particle effects and framework integrations.
tradeoff: Decorative effects should be bounded, optional, and absent from critical content paths.

category: 6. Motion, transitions, graphics, and creative rendering
name: Canvas Confetti
function: Short celebratory particle bursts.
tradeoff: Use for meaningful milestones; respect reduced motion and prevent repeat spam.

category: 6. Motion, transitions, graphics, and creative rendering
name: Remotion
function: Code-authored video composition, rendering, and player integration.
tradeoff: Useful for pre-rendered hero/demo assets; licensing differs by use and is not a generic animation-runtime license.

category: 6. Motion, transitions, graphics, and creative rendering
name: Blender
function: 3D modeling, materials, animation, lighting, and offline rendering for authentic assets.
tradeoff: Asset creation tool, not the browser runtime; optimize exports before web delivery.

category: 7. Components, design systems, and design workflow
name: Base UI
function: Unstyled React controls, menus, dialogs, comboboxes, navigation, and overlays.
tradeoff: Strong custom design-system foundation; check composition, portals, and focus in your app.

category: 7. Components, design systems, and design workflow
name: Radix Primitives
function: React primitives handling keyboard interaction, ARIA semantics, and focus management.
tradeoff: Mature option for existing products; styling and correct composition remain your responsibility.

category: 7. Components, design systems, and design workflow
name: React Aria
function: Accessible React behavior and components with internationalization and adaptive interaction.
tradeoff: Especially useful for complex selection, dates, and multilingual products; requires a visual layer.

category: 7. Components, design systems, and design workflow
name: Headless UI
function: Unstyled React/Vue menus, dialogs, listboxes, tabs, and related controls.
tradeoff: Good Tailwind fit; verify each framework's API and component availability.

category: 7. Components, design systems, and design workflow

function: Hosted media transformations and optimization/delivery; useful for large, changing media inventories.
tradeoff: Transformation policy, CDN caching, costs, data handling, and vendor dependence need explicit decisions.

category: 8. Platform, architecture, performance, accessibility, and QA reference

category: 8. Platform, architecture, performance, accessibility, and QA reference
